SJT-01.title: SJT-01 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-01.lead: You are leading a project team.
SJT-01.body_html: You are leading a project team. A senior colleague publicly contradicts your decision in a team meeting, suggesting your approach will fail. Several team members look uncomfortable. You have time to respond. How would you rank these responses from most to least appropriate?
characteristics: Clue: Consider emotional safety, professional respect, and decision-making authority. Which response prevents escalation while addressing the core issue?

SJT-02.title: SJT-02 (situational-judgement, hard)
SJT-02.lead: You discover a colleague has submitted work with data that appears to have been fabricated.
SJT-02.body_html: You discover a colleague has submitted work with data that appears to have been fabricated. You have no direct proof, only statistical implausibility. Your colleague is well-liked and has been at the organisation longer than you. Rate each response on a scale of 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Integrity matters, but so does due diligence and chain of command. What's the ethical path that respects both?

SJT-03.title: SJT-03 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-03.lead: Your team has a Friday afternoon deadline for a deliverable.
SJT-03.body_html: Your team has a Friday afternoon deadline for a deliverable. It's 2pm Thursday and you realise the project timeline was based on a misunderstanding of client requirements. Fixing it properly will take an extra 8 hours. Your team is already stretched. Rank these responses from most to least appropriate:
characteristics: Clue: Transparency, client value, and team sustainability all matter. What serves the client's true needs *and* protects the team?

SJT-04.title: SJT-04 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-04.lead: You're in a training session led by your director.
SJT-04.body_html: You're in a training session led by your director. You notice the content contains a significant factual error that contradicts established best practice. Several junior staff are present and taking notes. The session has 10 minutes remaining. Rate from 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Respect hierarchy, but junior staff are learning. How do you protect accuracy *and* the director's credibility?

SJT-05.title: SJT-05 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-05.lead: A team member has been chronically late to meetings and not completing assigned tasks.
SJT-05.body_html: A team member has been chronically late to meetings and not completing assigned tasks. Performance reviews are not for another month. They are a single parent dealing with childcare issues, which you know from casual conversation. You are not their manager, but you work closely with them. Rank from most to least appropriate:
characteristics: Clue: Compassion and accountability aren't opposites. What shows respect for their situation *and* the team's needs?

SJT-06.title: SJT-06 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-06.lead: You're working on a cross-functional project.
SJT-06.body_html: You're working on a cross-functional project. The Finance department submits a budget forecast that seems inconsistent with the operational data your team collected. There's a board meeting in 3 days where both forecasts will be presented. Rate from 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Collaboration + data integrity matter. What prevents a public misalignment while honoring both teams' work?

SJT-07.title: SJT-07 (situational-judgement, hard)
SJT-07.lead: A project is running 2 weeks behind schedule.
SJT-07.body_html: A project is running 2 weeks behind schedule. Your manager suggests cutting corner X (a quality assurance checkpoint) to recover time. You believe this checkpoint catches critical bugs. You have no data to quantify the risk, only professional judgement. Rank from most to least appropriate:
characteristics: Clue: Time and quality are both real constraints. What's the path that includes risk data *and* manager input?

SJT-08.title: SJT-08 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-08.lead: You overhear two colleagues gossiping about a third colleague's personal life—information that's neither job-relevant nor public.
SJT-08.body_html: You overhear two colleagues gossiping about a third colleague's personal life—information that's neither job-relevant nor public. They haven't noticed you're in the room. Rate from 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Personal dignity matters. What stops the gossip *and* helps the gossipers understand why?

SJT-09.title: SJT-09 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-09.lead: You're allocated a task that falls outside your expertise.
SJT-09.body_html: You're allocated a task that falls outside your expertise. The deadline is tight. Your manager assumes you'll figure it out. You could spend 8 hours learning, or 2 hours learning enough to delegate parts to someone with background. Rank from most to least appropriate:
characteristics: Clue: Consider deadline, skill gaps, and team capability. What's the fastest path that delivers *and* develops you?

SJT-10.title: SJT-10 (situational-judgement, hard)
SJT-10.body_html: Your organisation is downsizing. Your team will lose 20% of staff. You know which person is likely to be selected. They are a friend and a solid performer, but not the highest-performing member of the team. Rate from 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Loyalty to your friend and loyalty to your role are different. What respects both confidentiality *and* your responsibility?

SJT-11.title: SJT-11 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-11.lead: You're asked to join a working group on a strategic initiative.
SJT-11.body_html: You're asked to join a working group on a strategic initiative. Your schedule is already full, and you have doubts about the group's approach, but you respect the organiser. Rank from most to least appropriate:
characteristics: Clue: Respect + honesty coexist. When do you commit, when do you bow out, and when do you push back?

SJT-12.title: SJT-12 (situational-judgement, medium)
SJT-12.lead: A client sends you an email requesting something that's technically possible but would significantly increase project scope and cost.
SJT-12.body_html: A client sends you an email requesting something that's technically possible but would significantly increase project scope and cost. They seem unaware of the implications. You have a call with them in 2 days. Rate from 1 (most appropriate) to 5 (least appropriate):
characteristics: Clue: Transparency prevents conflict. What sets you up for a productive conversation?

VCR-01.title: VCR-01 (verbal-critical-reasoning, hard)
VCR-01.lead: The charity reported a 30% increase in donations last year.
VCR-01.body_html: The charity reported a 30% increase in donations last year. However, operational costs also rose by 25%. When adjusted for inflation, donations actually declined by 5% in real terms. Trustees attributed the nominal increase to a new social media campaign, but the timing doesn't match: the campaign launched in month 9 of the fiscal year, yet donation growth was strongest in months 1–3." Which of the following is an unstated assumption in the Trustees' attribution of donation growth to the social media campaign?
characteristics: Clue: The trustees attributed growth to the campaign. What must they be assuming to make that claim *despite the timing problem*?

VCR-02.title: VCR-02 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-02.lead: Studies show that people who exercise regularly report higher life satisfaction than sedentary people.
VCR-02.body_html: Studies show that people who exercise regularly report higher life satisfaction than sedentary people. Therefore, regular exercise is the cause of higher life satisfaction." Which of the following best identifies the logical flaw in this argument?
characteristics: Clue: The argument moves from "people who exercise *tend to* report higher satisfaction" to "exercise *causes* higher satisfaction." What's the logical leap?

VCR-03.title: VCR-03 (verbal-critical-reasoning, hard)
VCR-03.lead: Remote work has been shown to reduce office overhead costs by up to 40%.
VCR-03.body_html: Remote work has been shown to reduce office overhead costs by up to 40%. Critics worry that remote work reduces team cohesion and innovation. However, a survey of 500 remote workers found that 72% felt they were more productive at home than in the office. Therefore, organisations should adopt remote work policies." Which statement would most weaken the argument for remote-work adoption?
characteristics: Clue: The argument relies on a specific piece of evidence: worker surveys showing 72% higher productivity. What undermines *that evidence specifically*?

VCR-04.title: VCR-04 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-04.body_html: All successful entrepreneurs are risk-takers. Jane is a successful entrepreneur. Therefore, Jane is a risk-taker." Is this argument logically valid?
characteristics: Clue: Check the logical form: All X are Y. Jane is X. Therefore, Jane is Y. Is this form valid, regardless of whether the premises are true?

VCR-05.title: VCR-05 (verbal-critical-reasoning, hard)
VCR-05.lead: The school's reading proficiency scores improved by 8% after the district purchased new tablets for classroom use.
VCR-05.body_html: The school's reading proficiency scores improved by 8% after the district purchased new tablets for classroom use. The superintendent announced that technology investment is the key to student success." Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the superintendent's conclusion?
characteristics: Clue: The superintendent attributes the improvement to technology. What evidence would suggest the improvement wasn't due to the tablets at all?

VCR-06.title: VCR-06 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-06.lead: To be a doctor, one must complete medical school.
VCR-06.body_html: To be a doctor, one must complete medical school. Sarah is not in medical school. Therefore, Sarah is not a doctor." Is this argument logically valid?
characteristics: Clue: The form is: If X, then Y. Not Y. Therefore, not X. Is this a valid logical form?

VCR-07.title: VCR-07 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-07.lead: Renewable energy is essential for climate stability.
VCR-07.body_html: Renewable energy is essential for climate stability. Wind turbines are a form of renewable energy. Some windmills harm bird populations. Therefore, wind turbines are bad for the environment overall." Which statement best identifies the logical problem with this conclusion?
characteristics: Clue: The argument notes one negative (bird harm) and concludes wind turbines are "bad overall." What's the logical flaw?

VCR-08.title: VCR-08 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-08.lead: Company X increased salaries by 5% last year and saw employee turnover drop by 12%.
VCR-08.body_html: Company X increased salaries by 5% last year and saw employee turnover drop by 12%. The CEO credits the raise. However, the same year, Company X introduced flexible work arrangements, hired a new wellness coach, and redesigned office spaces for open collaboration." The argument that salary increases caused the drop in turnover is weakened by the fact that:
characteristics: Clue: Multiple changes happened at once. How does this affect the CEO's claim about what caused the turnover drop?

VCR-09.title: VCR-09 (verbal-critical-reasoning, hard)
VCR-09.lead: Studies prove that breakfast improves academic performance.
VCR-09.body_html: Studies prove that breakfast improves academic performance. Students who eat breakfast have higher grades than those who skip it. Therefore, all students should eat breakfast." Which assumption is necessary for the argument's conclusion to hold?
characteristics: Clue: The argument infers causation from a correlation. What must be assumed about alternative explanations?

VCR-10.title: VCR-10 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-10.body_html: No reptiles are warm-blooded. All mammals are warm-blooded. Snakes are reptiles. Therefore, snakes are not mammals." Is this argument logically valid?
characteristics: Clue: Check the logical form, ignoring real-world facts. Does the conclusion follow necessarily from the premises?

VCR-11.title: VCR-11 (verbal-critical-reasoning, hard)
VCR-11.lead: A study of 2,000 healthcare workers found that those who took regular breaks reported 34% fewer errors in patient care.
VCR-11.body_html: A study of 2,000 healthcare workers found that those who took regular breaks reported 34% fewer errors in patient care. The healthcare ministry recommends implementing mandatory 15-minute breaks every 2 hours based on this finding." The recommendation would be most strengthened if which additional information were available?
characteristics: Clue: The study shows correlation between breaks and fewer errors. What would make the *causal inference* more credible?

VCR-12.title: VCR-12 (verbal-critical-reasoning, medium)
VCR-12.lead: The new antibiotic kills 99.9% of the target bacteria in vitro.
VCR-12.body_html: The new antibiotic kills 99.9% of the target bacteria in vitro. Therefore, patients taking the antibiotic will recover quickly from bacterial infections." Which of the following best explains why the conclusion does not follow from the premise?
characteristics: Clue: Lab results ≠ real-world results. What's the key gap between test-tube and patient outcomes?

AR-01.title: AR-01 (abstract-reasoning, easy)
AR-01.lead: Each row is consistent in shape type.
AR-01.body_html: Each row is consistent in shape type. What shape belongs in the bottom row?
characteristics: Clue: Each row is consistent in shape type. What shape belongs in the bottom row?

AR-02.title: AR-02 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-02.body_html: Size increases down the rows. Position shifts across columns. Column 3 always has shapes where?
characteristics: Clue: Size increases down the rows. Position shifts across columns. Column 3 always has shapes where?

AR-03.title: AR-03 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-03.lead: Rotation increases by the same amount each time.
AR-03.body_html: Rotation increases by the same amount each time. What's the next rotation angle?
characteristics: Clue: Rotation increases by the same amount each time. What's the next rotation angle?

AR-04.title: AR-04 (abstract-reasoning, easy)
AR-04.lead: Four items share something in common; one breaks the pattern.
AR-04.body_html: Four items share something in common; one breaks the pattern. What property divides them?
characteristics: Clue: Four items share something in common; one breaks the pattern. What property divides them?

AR-05.title: AR-05 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-05.lead: Each row increases count from left to right.
AR-05.body_html: Each row increases count from left to right. Row 3 uses which shape, and what fill?
characteristics: Clue: Each row increases count from left to right. Row 3 uses which shape, and what fill?

AR-06.title: AR-06 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-06.lead: The dot moves along a path.
AR-06.body_html: The dot moves along a path. It started left, went center, then right. After the top-right, where's the logical next position?
characteristics: Clue: The dot moves along a path. It started left, went center, then right. After the top-right, where's the logical next position?

AR-07.title: AR-07 (abstract-reasoning, easy)
AR-07.lead: Column 2 is for one shape; Row 2 is for one fill type.
AR-07.body_html: Column 2 is for one shape; Row 2 is for one fill type. What's their intersection?
characteristics: Clue: Column 2 is for one shape; Row 2 is for one fill type. What's their intersection?

AR-08.title: AR-08 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-08.lead: Four items share a shape arrangement; one uses a different shape arrangement.
AR-08.body_html: Four items share a shape arrangement; one uses a different shape arrangement. What's different?
characteristics: Clue: Four items share a shape arrangement; one uses a different shape arrangement. What's different?

AR-09.title: AR-09 (abstract-reasoning, easy)
AR-09.body_html: Size has increased consistently. Following the pattern, the next size is...?
characteristics: Clue: Size has increased consistently. Following the pattern, the next size is...?

AR-10.title: AR-10 (abstract-reasoning, easy)
AR-10.body_html: Row 3 uses triangles. Column 2 has how many items?
characteristics: Clue: Row 3 uses triangles. Column 2 has how many items?

AR-11.title: AR-11 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-11.body_html: Rotation increases 45° per step. After 135°, the next is...?
characteristics: Clue: Rotation increases 45° per step. After 135°, the next is...?

AR-12.title: AR-12 (abstract-reasoning, medium)
AR-12.lead: Four items arrange dots in a closed geometric shape; one uses an open arrangement.
AR-12.body_html: Four items arrange dots in a closed geometric shape; one uses an open arrangement. Which is different?
characteristics: Clue: Four items arrange dots in a closed geometric shape; one uses an open arrangement. Which is different?

DAR-01.title: DAR-01 (deductive-analytical, easy)
DAR-01.body_html: All cats are animals. Some animals are furry. Mittens is a cat." Which of the following must be true?
characteristics: Clue: What can you deduce with certainty from "All cats are animals" + "Mittens is a cat"?

DAR-02.title: DAR-02 (deductive-analytical, medium)
DAR-02.lead: If a person studies regularly, they will pass the exam.
DAR-02.body_html: If a person studies regularly, they will pass the exam. If a person passes the exam, they will graduate. Sarah studied regularly." Which conclusion follows logically?
characteristics: Clue: Chain the two conditional statements together. If Sarah studies, what can you conclude at the end?

DAR-03.title: DAR-03 (deductive-analytical, medium)
DAR-03.body_html: All humans are mortal. Socrates is human. Therefore, Socrates is mortal." Is this argument logically valid? If so, can you identify the logical form?
characteristics: Clue: Check the structure: All X are Y; Z is X; therefore Z is Y. Is this a valid form?

DAR-04.title: DAR-04 (deductive-analytical, easy)
DAR-04.lead: To get a driver's license, you must pass a written test and a driving test.
DAR-04.body_html: To get a driver's license, you must pass a written test and a driving test. Alex passed the written test but failed the driving test." Which of the following can be concluded?
characteristics: Clue: What condition is necessary to get a license? Does Alex meet all necessary conditions?

DAR-05.title: DAR-05 (deductive-analytical, hard)
DAR-05.body_html: Some lawyers are dishonest. All politicians are either lawyers or business owners. No business owners are dishonest." Which of the following must be true?
characteristics: Clue: Politicians are either lawyers or business owners. Business owners aren't dishonest. What can you infer about politicians?

DAR-06.title: DAR-06 (deductive-analytical, hard)
DAR-06.lead: Sufficient condition: If it's raining, then the ground is wet.
DAR-06.body_html: Sufficient condition: If it's raining, then the ground is wet. Necessary condition: The ground is wet only if it has rained or someone watered it." Which of the following correctly distinguishes sufficient from necessary?
characteristics: Clue: Sufficient = if this, then that. Necessary = can't have one without the other. Which is raining?

DAR-07.title: DAR-07 (deductive-analytical, hard)
DAR-07.lead: All employees at Company X work Monday–Friday.
DAR-07.body_html: All employees at Company X work Monday–Friday. Some part-time employees are not full-time. Some part-time employees work Monday–Friday." Can you conclude: "Some part-time employees at Company X work Monday–Friday"?
characteristics: Clue: The premises tell us about (1) Company X employees (Mon–Fri), (2) part-time employees generally, and (3) part-time employees (Mon–Fri). Are we told any overlap between Company X and part-time?

DAR-08.title: DAR-08 (deductive-analytical, medium)
DAR-08.lead: If the project is approved, funding is released.
DAR-08.body_html: If the project is approved, funding is released. If funding is released, development starts. If development starts, a prototype is built. If the project is not approved, the team is reassigned." If the prototype is built, what can we infer with certainty?
characteristics: Clue: Work backward from "prototype is built." What had to happen before?

DAR-09.title: DAR-09 (deductive-analytical, hard)
DAR-09.lead: No one who is qualified is rejected.
DAR-09.body_html: No one who is qualified is rejected. Everyone who applies is either qualified or under-qualified. Sarah was rejected." What must be true about Sarah?
characteristics: Clue: Sarah was rejected. If she applied, she must have been under-qualified (since qualified people aren't rejected). Did she apply?

DAR-10.title: DAR-10 (deductive-analytical, easy)
DAR-10.lead: To attend the gala, you must have an invitation or be a member.
DAR-10.body_html: To attend the gala, you must have an invitation or be a member. To be a member, you must pay the annual fee and pass a background check. James paid the fee but did not pass the background check." Can James attend the gala?
characteristics: Clue: What are the two ways to attend? Can James satisfy one of them?

DAR-11.title: DAR-11 (deductive-analytical, medium)
DAR-11.lead: All winners of the championship are experienced players.
DAR-11.body_html: All winners of the championship are experienced players. Most experienced players have trained for years. Not all trained players become winners." Which statement is necessarily true?
characteristics: Clue: What's required for winning? What can you say about all winners?

DAR-12.title: DAR-12 (deductive-analytical, medium)
DAR-12.lead: Promotion requires either 5 years of experience or a relevant degree.
DAR-12.body_html: Promotion requires either 5 years of experience or a relevant degree. Not all employees have relevant degrees. All employees with 5+ years of experience are promoted." Which of the following could be true?
characteristics: Clue: Requirements for promotion are: (5+ years) OR (degree). Which scenario satisfies one of these?

DIR-01.title: DIR-01 (data-interpretation, medium)
DIR-01.body_html: ``` TABLE: Regional Sales by Quarter (in £1000s) Region | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 North | 120 | 140 | 155 | 160 South | 100 | 110 | 105 | 115 East | 90 | 100 | 130 | 125 West | 110 | 115 | 120 | 135 TOTALS: Q1=420, Q2=465, Q3=510, Q4=535 ``` Which region showed the most volatile (inconsistent) growth across the four quarters?
characteristics: Clue: Calculate the quarter-to-quarter changes for each region. Which has the biggest swings?

DIR-02.title: DIR-02 (data-interpretation, easy)
DIR-02.lead: ``` TABLE: Customer Retention Rates (%) Year | Cohort A | Cohort B | Cohort C | Cohort D 2020 | 100%     | 100%     | —        | — 2021 | 92%      | 94%      | 100%     | — 2022 | 85%      | 88%      | 96%      | 100% 2023 | 78%      | 82%
DIR-02.body_html: ``` TABLE: Customer Retention Rates (%) Year | Cohort A | Cohort B | Cohort C | Cohort D 2020 | 100% | 100% | — | — 2021 | 92% | 94% | 100% | — 2022 | 85% | 88% | 96% | 100% 2023 | 78% | 82% | 89% | 97% 2024 | 72% | 76% | 82% | 93% Note: Each cohort starts at 100% and is tracked for up to 5 years. ``` Which cohort has experienced the least customer retention loss as a percentage of starting population?
characteristics: Clue: Loss = 100% − (final retention rate). Which cohort retained the highest percentage?

DIR-03.title: DIR-03 (data-interpretation, medium)
DIR-03.lead: ``` CHART: Average Monthly Rainfall (mm) by Month Month    | Rainfall January  | 45 February | 40 March    | 50 April    | 75 May      | 120 June     | 150 July     | 140 August   | 130 September| 90 October  | 60 November | 50 December | 4
DIR-03.body_html: ``` CHART: Average Monthly Rainfall (mm) by Month Month | Rainfall January | 45 February | 40 March | 50 April | 75 May | 120 June | 150 July | 140 August | 130 September| 90 October | 60 November | 50 December | 45 Total annual: 945 mm ``` In which consecutive 3-month period does the highest concentration of rainfall occur?
characteristics: Clue: Sum each rolling 3-month window. Which has the largest sum?

DIR-04.title: DIR-04 (data-interpretation, hard)
DIR-04.lead: ``` TABLE: Employee Salaries by Department Department | Count | Total Salary | Average Salary HR         | 5     | £150,000     | £30,000 IT         | 12    | £600,000     | £50,000 Marketing  | 8     | £240,000     | £30,000 Operations | 1
DIR-04.body_html: ``` TABLE: Employee Salaries by Department Department | Count | Total Salary | Average Salary HR | 5 | £150,000 | £30,000 IT | 12 | £600,000 | £50,000 Marketing | 8 | £240,000 | £30,000 Operations | 10 | £350,000 | £35,000 Finance | 7 | £280,000 | £40,000 Company Total: 42 employees, £1,620,000 total salary ``` What is the median salary (the salary at the 50th percentile) across all 42 employees?
characteristics: Clue: To find the median, you need to order all individual salaries and find the middle value. Can you do this with only departmental averages?

DIR-05.title: DIR-05 (data-interpretation, medium)
DIR-05.lead: ``` TABLE: Product Sales and Profit Margins Product | Units Sold | Price/Unit | Revenue | Profit Margin A       | 500        | £40        | £20,000 | 20% B       | 300        | £60        | £18,000 | 25% C       | 1,200      | £10        |
DIR-05.body_html: ``` TABLE: Product Sales and Profit Margins Product | Units Sold | Price/Unit | Revenue | Profit Margin A | 500 | £40 | £20,000 | 20% B | 300 | £60 | £18,000 | 25% C | 1,200 | £10 | £12,000 | 30% D | 200 | £75 | £15,000 | 40% Total Revenue: £65,000 ``` Which product contributes the most to total profit (absolute value, not margin %)?
characteristics: Clue: Profit = Revenue × Margin %. Multiply for each product and compare.

DIR-06.title: DIR-06 (data-interpretation, easy)
DIR-06.lead: ``` CHART: Website Traffic by Device Type Device      | Feb 2024 | Mar 2024 | Apr 2024 | May 2024 Desktop     | 5,000    | 5,200    | 5,100    | 4,900 Mobile      | 8,000    | 8,500    | 9,200    | 10,100 Tablet      | 1,500    | 1,400    |
DIR-06.body_html: ``` CHART: Website Traffic by Device Type Device | Feb 2024 | Mar 2024 | Apr 2024 | May 2024 Desktop | 5,000 | 5,200 | 5,100 | 4,900 Mobile | 8,000 | 8,500 | 9,200 | 10,100 Tablet | 1,500 | 1,400 | 1,300 | 1,200 Total Traffic: 14,500 (Feb) | 15,100 (Mar) | 15,600 (Apr) | 16,200 (May) ``` What is the percentage of total traffic from Mobile devices in May 2024?
characteristics: Clue: Percentage = (Mobile traffic ÷ Total traffic) × 100. Calculate for May.

DIR-07.title: DIR-07 (data-interpretation, easy)
DIR-07.lead: ``` TABLE: Student Test Scores (out of 100) Class A: 78, 82, 85, 88, 90, 92 Class B: 55, 70, 75, 80, 85, 95 Statistical Summary: Class A: Mean=86, Median=87, Range=14 Class B: Mean=77, Median=77.5, Range=40 ``` Which class has more consiste
DIR-07.body_html: ``` TABLE: Student Test Scores (out of 100) Class A: 78, 82, 85, 88, 90, 92 Class B: 55, 70, 75, 80, 85, 95 Statistical Summary: Class A: Mean=86, Median=87, Range=14 Class B: Mean=77, Median=77.5, Range=40 ``` Which class has more consistent (less spread) scores, and what metric best shows this?
characteristics: Clue: Consistency = low spread. Range = max − min. Smaller range = more consistent.

DIR-08.title: DIR-08 (data-interpretation, easy)
DIR-08.lead: ``` TABLE: Store Inventory and Turnover Rates Product | Stock Units | Monthly Sales | Turnover Rate X       | 100         | 50            | 0.5 per month Y       | 200         | 120           | 0.6 per month Z       | 150         | 90
DIR-08.body_html: ``` TABLE: Store Inventory and Turnover Rates Product | Stock Units | Monthly Sales | Turnover Rate X | 100 | 50 | 0.5 per month Y | 200 | 120 | 0.6 per month Z | 150 | 90 | 0.6 per month Turnover rate = Monthly sales ÷ Stock units ``` If stock levels remain constant and turnover rates hold steady, approximately how many units of Product Y will be sold in 12 months?
characteristics: Clue: Monthly sales = 120. Annual sales = monthly × 12 months.

DIR-09.title: DIR-09 (data-interpretation, medium)
DIR-09.lead: ``` TABLE: Budget Allocation ($) Department | 2023 Budget | 2024 Budget | Change Engineering| 500,000     | 550,000     | +50,000 Marketing  | 200,000     | 220,000     | +20,000 Operations | 300,000     | 315,000     | +15,000 Admin      |
DIR-09.body_html: ``` TABLE: Budget Allocation ($) Department | 2023 Budget | 2024 Budget | Change Engineering| 500,000 | 550,000 | +50,000 Marketing | 200,000 | 220,000 | +20,000 Operations | 300,000 | 315,000 | +15,000 Admin | 100,000 | 105,000 | +5,000 Total 2023: $1,100,000 Total 2024: $1,190,000 ``` Which department received the largest percentage increase?
characteristics: Clue: Percentage increase = (Change ÷ Original) × 100. Calculate for each.

DIR-10.title: DIR-10 (data-interpretation, medium)
DIR-10.lead: ``` TABLE: Customer Feedback Scores (1–5 scale) Metric              | Q1  | Q2  | Q3  | Q4 Product Quality     | 4.2 | 4.3 | 4.1 | 4.4 Customer Service    | 3.8 | 3.9 | 4.1 | 4.2 Delivery Speed      | 3.5 | 3.6 | 3.7 | 3.9 Value for Money

DIR-11.body_html: ``` TABLE: Project Budget Variance Phase | Budgeted | Actual | Variance Design | 50,000 | 48,000 | −2,000 (under budget) Development| 200,000 | 220,000| +20,000 (over budget) Testing | 80,000 | 85,000 | +5,000 (over budget) Deployment | 30,000 | 31,000 | +1,000 (over budget) Total Budgeted: 360,000 Total Actual: 384,000 Overall Variance: +24,000 (9% over budget) ``` Development's variance (+£20,000) represents what percentage of the total project budget overspend?
characteristics: Clue: Total overspend = £24,000. Development's overspend = £20,000. What % of total overspend is that?

DIR-12.title: DIR-12 (data-interpretation, hard)
DIR-12.lead: ``` TABLE: Subscription Revenue Model Tier | Monthly Fee | Subscribers | Monthly Revenue Free | £0          | 5,000       | £0 Basic| £5          | 2,000       | £10,000 Pro  | £15         | 800         | £12,000 Enterprise| £50    | 150
DIR-12.body_html: ``` TABLE: Subscription Revenue Model Tier | Monthly Fee | Subscribers | Monthly Revenue Free | £0 | 5,000 | £0 Basic| £5 | 2,000 | £10,000 Pro | £15 | 800 | £12,000 Enterprise| £50 | 150 | £7,500 Total Subscribers: 7,950 Total Revenue: £29,500 ``` If the company shifts 300 Basic subscribers to Pro (at no additional cost as an upgrade), what is the new monthly revenue?
characteristics: Clue: 300 Basic subscribers leave (lose 300 × £5 = −£1,500). They become Pro (gain 300 × £15 = +£4,500). Net change = +£3,000.
